To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a suite of methods for designing genome-specific or tissue- specific biochips using short oligo probes to identify genes with differential expression between two or more samples and that these methods have been tested using yeast ORFs.

we have designed a set of short 8mers to identify genes that are expressed at least 2.5-fold different between two samples and have shown that this method can identify genes that are known to be differentially expressed.
the use of a relatively small set of short probes can be used for gene-expression profiling and that this approach is applicable to other organisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of biochips for genome- or tissue-specific gene expression studies.
the design of short oligo biochips and the use of the biochips for whole-genome differential gene-expression profiling.
the development of new algorithms to identify genes that are expressed differentially between two samples and to design a genome- or tissue-specific bio-chip.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have developed a set of methods that can be used for genome- or tissue-specific gene-expressions studies.
our methods can be used to design genome or tissue-specific short probes to identify genes with differential expression between samples.
our method is a powerful and effective tool to design a genome-wide biochip for differential gene-expression profiling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a set of methods to design a set of short probes to identify genes differentially expressed in a set of samples.
the use of short oligo probe arrays can be a powerful tool for genome-scale gene expression studies.
a relatively small number (4,000 in this work) of short probes are capable of identifying differentially expressed genes in the whole-genome level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to use a small number of short probes to perform whole-genome or genome-specific gene-expression studies at a fraction of the cost of the standard gene chips.
a small set of short probes can be used to identify differentially expressed genes between samples.
the combinatorial use of a small number of short probes for gene-expression analysis is feasible and can be a cost-effective alternative to gene chips.
